note: The outcome every verification lane produced when this ceiling was recorded. The matrix fails when a lane produces a worse outcome than the one recorded here, when a recorded lane disappears, when a lane appears that this file does not record, or when any lane actually fails. A lane sitting at its recorded outcome does not fail the build, so a known hole stays visible without holding a required check red; improving a lane never fails it either. Editing this file is the only sanctioned way to record a worse outcome, so a deliberate one leaves a reviewable diff and a silent one turns the matrix red.
claim_note: A recorded outcome says what the lane did, not that what it did was sufficient. Two of these ten lanes executed nothing they were named for.

evaluator-all-suites.note: 24 of the 27 declared eval suites report not_applicable and execute nothing. The suite status ceiling recorded beside the registry is what stops that number growing; this lane is partial rather than pass so the matrix never reports 27 suites of coverage when it has 3.

node.note: No root package.json exists, so the node lane runs nothing, while apps/web, packages/ui and scripts/brand are npm workspaces with lockfiles. The lane cannot simply be switched on: apps/web/app/page.tsx renders LeaderboardFirstPrototype from the ui package and apps/web/app/globals.css imports its stylesheet, but packages/ui/src/concepts/leaderboard-first.css has never existed in git, so the home page has never rendered. The component carries 46 class-name uses on an lf- prefixed system and its sibling stylesheet is 235 lines, so authoring it is design work rather than a mechanical repair, and the alternative is deciding to delete the concept. That decision is tracked and unmade. Recording the hole keeps it visible and makes it impossible for a second lane to go dark unnoticed.
